C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY.Name: Engine parity for the search zone — one semantic table, one flag source, explicit case mode, gitignore outside git, boundary-safe truncation — implementation plan
C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY.IntentSummary: Close the recorded engine-parity debt of the search zone in src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs: one documented engine-parity table (a paired file-local block) governs the embedded ignore/regex walker and the rg shell-out across all four transport legs (content walker, files walker, content rg search, rg files listing); one shared flag-resolution artifact (fn resolve_engine_flags, one START_CONTRACT block) becomes the only place where the shared engine semantics are chosen — both WalkBuilder chains and both rg command builders draw from it, per-leg leftovers are only the legs' inherent shape (rg process arguments versus ignore-crate builder calls) and the documented files-mode size row. The case mode becomes explicit-option-only on both engines: the pattern-dependent --smart-case implicit branch is removed from the rg content transport and replaced by the explicit insensitive default (--ignore-case) with --case-sensitive on the toggle, making the walker's build_matcher semantics (:671-673) the canon unchanged; the renderer's isCaseSensitive toggle is the only case control and no renderer file is written. .gitignore handling outside a git repository becomes identical on both engines: both rg transports (START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_COMMAND, START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_FILES_COMMAND) gain --no-require-git through the shared flag source, making the walker legs' "(matches ripgrep --no-require-git)" comments (:576, :834) true without touching a walker line. The content walker's byte-offset snippet truncation stops panicking on multi-byte content — the cut floors to the last UTF-8 character boundary at or before MAX_LINE_BYTES (closes the recorded triple-debt entry named verbatim in the NonGoals of C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY #303, C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD #324 and C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE #333) — pinned by a failing-first Cyrillic/emoji regression test. A parameterized parity suite runs one fixture set through both engines with identical expectations per table row (case modes, gitignore outside git, hidden files, exclusion masks, maxFileSize content row, follow, whole-word, literal), with the rg legs under the existing availability guard. The files-mode per-transport size divergence is resolved in the table as documentation: the walker metadata skip stays canon, the rg --files listing stays not size-filtered, and the delivery-baseline comment at the files-command block is updated to point at the table row. Session machinery, engine selection, wire envelope, the #303 honesty machinery and the #320 bounds contract are consumed unchanged.

T-001.Title: Failing-first parity pins: the case-mode divergence, the gitignore-outside divergence, the UTF-8 cap-crossing panic, and the agreeing-row insurance suite

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add the four named inline #[cfg(test)] tests in src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs and record their receipts against the pre-change tree BEFORE implementing, red exactly as described — receipts preserved as pre-change evidence in the change record, never relabeled post-fix. (a) engine_parity_case_modes_across_legs — one TempDir fixture whose lines contain "needle", "NEEDLE" and "Needle"; with default options and the Mixed-case pattern "Needle" the test asserts the walker leg (always run) and the rg leg (under the existing rg_available guard with the canon skip marker) return the IDENTICAL result set covering all three case variants: today the walker returns three variants and rg's --smart-case returns only the exact-case line, so the test is red as a result-set mismatch; the same fixture with isCaseSensitive true asserts only the exact line on both legs (green today, green after); a lowercase-pattern case on the same fixture asserts the #320 parity shape (green today, green after — smart-case is insensitive for an all-lowercase pattern exactly like the walker default). (b) engine_parity_gitignore_outside_git_across_legs — a TempDir fixture with NO .git entry, a .gitignore listing one file, and a sibling file, both bodies containing the needle: content mode AND files mode are searched on both engines and the gitignored file is absent while the sibling is present identically on every leg; today the walker legs filter and the rg legs do not, so the test is red as a result-set mismatch; a companion assertion searches a git-repository fixture (the root carries a .git directory — the same presence heuristic the ignore crate and rg consult for require_git; no git binary invocation, no PATH mutation) and asserts both engines filter identically there — green before and after, recording that inside a git repository nothing changes.

(c) walker_utf8_boundary_truncation_does_not_panic — a walker-leg fixture whose line byte length exceeds MAX_LINE_BYTES and whose multi-byte characters straddle the cap offset (1-byte filler up to MAX_LINE_BYTES minus one, then Cyrillic letters and an emoji, then the needle — so the byte cut at MAX_LINE_BYTES lands inside a multi-byte character): today the byte slice at :894 panics and the test is red BY PANIC; the test catches nothing by hand — it asserts the session completes — and pins: no panic, the hit delivered, truncated true, the ellipsis marker present, the delivered snippet valid UTF-8 (String::from_utf8 on the wire form) and no longer than MAX_LINE_BYTES plus the marker bytes, and honest-or-absent bounds per the #320 rule (a match not fully inside the delivered text stays wire-absent, pinned via serde_json serialization).

(d) engine_parity_hidden_and_excludes_across_legs — the agreeing-row insurance suite over one fixture set: hidden files (default skip and include_hidden picks the dotfile up), exclusion masks (a masked file absent, an unmasked sibling present, an invalid mask ignored on both legs while forcing the session partial flag), the content-mode maxFileSize row (a size-limited fixture yields identically filtered results on both legs), follow_symlinks, whole-word and literal/regex shapes — each row asserted identically on the walker leg (always) and the rg leg (availability-guarded); green before AND after by construction — the pin exists so the implementation tasks cannot silently break an agreeing row while re-plumbing flags.

At this point every neighbor suite named in the ReferenceState stays green verbatim and unweakened (case_insensitive_default :1779, case_sensitive_excludes_mismatched_case :1793, gitignore_excluded_files_skipped :1821, no_ignore_includes_gitignored_files :1834, hidden_files_skipped_by_default :1983, include_hidden_picks_up_dotfiles :1995, rg_exit_two_is_single_error_terminal :2314, exclusions_applied_symmetrically :2485, invalid_exclusion_mask_is_ignored_and_forces_partial :2559, the #320 bounds family :3283/:3324/:3414/:3447 and the #333 files-mode family :3620/:3718/:3843/:3942/:4108/:4188); no production code changes in this task — tests only; no PATH mutation, no network, no git binary invocation, no new sleeps beyond the established collect_until_terminal timeouts.

T-002.Title: Case-mode parity: the shared flag-resolution artifact introduced, --smart-case removed, explicit --ignore-case/--case-sensitive by option on the rg leg

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Introduce the one shared flag-resolution artifact fn resolve_engine_flags (one paired START_CONTRACT: resolve_engine_flags / END_CONTRACT: resolve_engine_flags block): it resolves the shared engine semantics from SearchOptions exactly once — case mode (explicit-option-only: insensitive by default, sensitive on the isCaseSensitive toggle), gitignore-outside (the require_git(false) canon, consumed by T-003), hidden, the ignore-family switch (no_ignore), follow_symlinks, whole-word, literal/regex, exclusions and max_file_size per mode — and it is the only place those decisions are made. Both WalkBuilder chains (content :825-838, files path leg :567-580) and both rg command builders (START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_COMMAND :1109-1145, START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_FILES_COMMAND :1413-1446) consume it; per-leg leftovers are only the legs' inherent shape (rg argument spelling versus ignore-crate builder calls) and the documented files-mode size row (the rg --files listing keeps skipping the size flag). The T-002 slice moves the case row through the artifact; the remaining rows resolve to today's values (refactor-only — the agreeing-row suites of T-001(d) prove no drift); T-003 completes the artifact's gitignore row.

The rg content transport's case branch is replaced: the --smart-case argument disappears from the command assembly (cmd.arg("--smart-case"); no longer exists in the file) and resolve_engine_flags's case decision feeds an explicit --case-sensitive when the toggle is true, an explicit --ignore-case otherwise — the walker's explicit-option semantics become the canon on both engines. build_matcher keeps case_insensitive(!opts.is_case_sensitive.unwrap_or(false)) unchanged (:671-673) and no walker line changes. engine_parity_case_modes_across_legs turns green: the Mixed-case default case now yields all three variants identically on both legs; case_insensitive_default :1779 and case_sensitive_excludes_mismatched_case :1793 stay green verbatim; bounds_parity_across_engines :3324 stays green (its fixture uses a lowercase pattern, whose behavior is identical before and after).

Nothing else moves: the block structure of both rg transports, the spawn machinery, the #303 exit gate (:1348-1358), bounded stderr capture, both cancel watchers, batching and DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, the mt::search-event envelope (kinds match/complete/cancelled/error, additive optional partial, additive optional matchStart/matchEnd), M-010 root validation, engine selection (:990-999), the 120 ms warm-up and the registry lifecycle stay byte-for-byte; no new rg flag beyond the case-mode replacement arguments; no new SearchOptions field, rename or wire shape; no renderer file is written and the renderer's isCaseSensitive toggle keeps its name, default and store wiring. The engine-parity table is started as file-local documentation under a paired // START_BLOCK_ENGINE_PARITY_TABLE / // END_BLOCK_ENGINE_PARITY_TABLE marker with the case row filled (semantic, the two anchors, and the recorded removal reason: smart-case's implicit pattern-dependence overrode the explicit toggle on the rg leg only and was the divergence source).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Both rg transports pass --no-require-git (as .arg("--no-require-git") in the content command builder and in the files listing command builder), resolved through resolve_engine_flags's gitignore decision — no per-leg hardcoded gitignore flag remains outside the artifact. Inside a git repository no behavior changes on either engine (the companion assertion of T-001(b) stays green).

engine_parity_gitignore_outside_git_across_legs turns green: the no-git fixture filters identically on all four legs (content walker, content rg, files walker, files rg — gitignored absent, sibling present); the .ignore semantics are unaffected on both engines (rg honors .ignore regardless of git presence, matching the walker's .ignore switch) and no_ignore keeps disabling all ignore sources on both engines: gitignore_excluded_files_skipped :1821, no_ignore_includes_gitignored_files :1834, hidden_files_skipped_by_default :1983 and include_hidden_picks_up_dotfiles :1995 stay green verbatim; rg_exit_two_is_single_error_terminal :2314 stays green (the honesty machinery was not touched).

The parity table gains the gitignore row: inside-git and outside-git columns, the walker anchor (:576/:834) and both rg anchors, and --no-require-git recorded as the delivered flag making the walker comment true; the .ignore row and the no_ignore row are documented on the same pass (they already agree; the table records them with their anchors).

T-004.Title: Boundary-safe snippet truncation: floor the cut to the last UTF-8 character boundary at or before MAX_LINE_BYTES

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The snippet construction site (:892-897) stops byte-slicing at a raw offset: a local helper fn floor_to_char_boundary (documented as flooring the cut to the last UTF-8 character boundary at or before the cap) is applied before slicing, so the delivered snippet is the longest prefix of the line ending on a char boundary at or before MAX_LINE_BYTES — at most three bytes shorter than today's intended byte cut, never longer; the raw slicing expression "&line[..MAX_LINE_BYTES.min(line.len())]" no longer exists in the file. The cap value MAX_LINE_BYTES (:91) stays a byte cap and unchanged (the V-M-004 "no full-line buffer over 4 MB" budget holds); the ellipsis marker, the truncated flag, delivered_end_byte and the honest-or-absent bounds rule keep their contracts; byte_offset_to_utf16_units (:154) is not edited.

walker_utf8_boundary_truncation_does_not_panic turns green: the Cyrillic/emoji cap-crossing fixture completes without panic, delivers the hit with truncated true and the ellipsis marker, the snippet is valid UTF-8 and no longer than MAX_LINE_BYTES plus the marker bytes, and the bounds follow the honest-or-absent rule; match_beyond_truncated_snippet_yields_absent_bounds (:3414) stays green verbatim with its ASCII fixture.

The truncation change is local to the content walker's body-scan leg: the files-mode path-only legs stay body-read-free (the START_BLOCK_WALKER_PATH_LEG contract :550-556 — truncation does not apply to them) and the rg content transport's delivery shape is unchanged (rg lines are not walker-capped; no new truncation is introduced there). The parity table gains the truncation row: the walker cap as walker-inherent behavior, the rg delivery as rg-inherent, the closing of the recorded triple-debt entry (the UTF-8 truncation item named verbatim in the NonGoals of #303, #324 and #333) noted with the failing-first receipt reference.

T-005.Title: The parameterized parity suite: one fixture set, both engines, identical expectations per table row, one flag source provable

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The T-001 named tests are consolidated into the parameterized suite shaped after files_mode_rg_parity_with_walker_on_one_fixture (:4108): one shared fixture-builder feeds every table row through BOTH engines — the walker leg always (in_process = true, the App Store and missing-rg paths), the rg leg under the existing availability guard with the canon skip marker — with identical expected sets per row: case modes (default and toggle-on, including the Mixed-case pattern), gitignore outside git (content mode and files mode), hidden files (default skip and include_hidden), exclusion masks (valid masked-absent/sibling-present and invalid-ignored-with-partial), the content-mode maxFileSize row, follow_symlinks, whole-word and literal/regex; the UTF-8 truncation row remains the walker-leg regression pin (the 1 MB cap is walker-inherent; the rg leg's delivery shape is documented in the table, not equated). The gitignore row covers all four legs (content and files modes). The suite fails loudly if one leg's aligned row is edited without the other — that is its construction: identical expectations from one fixture.

The named tests keep their spec names and assertions through the consolidation — engine_parity_case_modes_across_legs, engine_parity_gitignore_outside_git_across_legs, walker_utf8_boundary_truncation_does_not_panic and engine_parity_hidden_and_excludes_across_legs are not relabeled, skipped or weakened, and the T-001 red receipts stay recorded as pre-change evidence. Availability-guard discipline: on machines without rg the rg-leg rows skip with the canon marker and the walker rows always run; no test mutates PATH or any process-global, adds no network, and adds no sleeps beyond the established collect_until_terminal timeouts.

The one-flag-source property is provable: the file-local contract of resolve_engine_flags names it as the single flag authority for the aligned rows; after T-002..T-004 no per-leg hardcoded case or gitignore flag remains outside it in any of the four build sites; the parity table's rows carry the owning anchor per leg; the files-command block's size note (:1414-1419) is updated to point at the delivered table row (the phrase "files-mode size row" names it) while keeping the safety argument — quickOpen never sends maxFileSize in files mode — and the walker metadata skip stays canon with no --max-filesize added to the listing transport on this change's authority. All neighbor pins from the ReferenceState stay green verbatim and unweakened.
